# A 40.00 invoice naming the deposit an unpost left loose, and declaring the
# 60.00 it does not take.
#
# The money is not the customer's credit — a bank paid it, and it is waiting to
# be put back — so what is left over after this invoice takes its 40.00 is
# still that. Dividing it must leave the remaining 60.00 marked as the
# settlement it is, and must not open a cost basis for it: the basis of the
# document that deposit settled sits on that document's posting split, and
# pricing the residue at *this* invoice's rate would report a gain the
# customer's money never made.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-SMALLER"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-03-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-03-01
		description: "Small job"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 40
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-03-01
		due: 2026-04-01
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-SMALLER"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-02-25
		amount: 100
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		prepayment: 60
		memo: "Part of the deposit"
